report: Reviewed the complete claim, both ordinary implementation associations (parser.rs and validate.rs), and both ordinary tests. Independently verified exact byte equality of both implementation files and both containing test files against the supplied historical input; reassessed the supplied historical rationale against current evidence. Parser::type_declaration shares parameter parsing across struct, enum and opaque forms: after '<' it requires one identifier, consumes comma-separated identifiers and requires '>', establishing a nonempty bracketed list. check_values passes only each owning declaration's parameter vector to resolution of struct fields and enum named/tuple fields; recursive resolution retains that vector. build_model registers declaration names/arity, not parameter names, and class contexts use an empty parameter vector. Thus parameters remain available within their declaration without leaking globally; opaque declarations have no representation fields. parameters_are_local_to_struct_enum_and_opaque_declarations asserts the exact T/U vector for all three forms, successful validation of parameter uses and concrete applications, and exactly one unknown-type-T diagnostic when a subsequent declaration attempts to use T. rejects_malformed_value_declarations explicitly rejects struct Bad<>; its other malformed cases cover neighboring requirements. Together these assertions and shared parser/resolver paths substantiate syntax, all declaration forms, local availability and non-leakage; dropping a parameter or leaking it would fail visible assertions. Captured parse_body/check helpers and language test imports via review read; helper assertions remain visible in the associated test itself. No TODO or N/A entries or deferral prerequisites exist. Source inspection supports no requested edits. Execution: I ran review start, review read and exact-comparison commands, and am recording this report; I did not run behavior tests or builds.
